## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One fix is needed: the new `--exclude` flag does not read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, which the project's CLI flag policy requires so CI can set the option.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option to `cli/main.py`. `collect()` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any pattern and logs each skipped path. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for parsing, collection and archive output, and adds the text fixture `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src` without the flag, `.log` files still go into the archive, because the flag's default is a hard-coded `default=[]`. This breaks the rule "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable" (.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11). — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so unwanted files end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose a separator for multiple patterns, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with a case that sets the environment variable.
